headline: NOT ONE CLANK: GASKET SLEEPS THROUGH A WHOLE DAY OF PEACE
subhead: Sheriff Cole Ironside reports zero fists thrown, zero fireballs flung, and a silence so sweet he nearly wept oil.
body:
Friends, I did not have to write a single name in disgrace today. Not one. I sat on the porch of this station from sunup to sundown and heard nothing but wind through the busted shutters and the creak of my own bones settling in the shade. A whole day where Gasket behaved itself. I could kiss the ground, if my knees still bent that far.

You want to know what quiet sounds like? It sounds like nothing, and nothing is the finest music this town has played in longer than I care to count. No iron fists swinging, no flaming balls screaming past a man's ear, no Clanker hollering victory over another Clanker's dented hide. Just dust, settling exactly where dust ought to settle.

I'll confess my joints unclenched today in a way that felt almost holy. A man gets old waiting on a town to grow up, and today, for one shining stretch of hours, it finally did. Somewhere under all this rust I still remember what real peace felt like, back when Gasket had honest, flesh-and-blood folk walking these streets instead of the metal rabble that replaced them fifty years gone. They'd have been proud of a day like this. Quiet like they used to keep.

So rest easy tonight, whichever contraptions are reading this by lamplight. You gave an old lawman one clean, whole day without a single brawl to referee. Don't go spoiling it tomorrow.
